title: An inert output cone is relatively limiting for an operad map
statement:
Use symmetric infinity-operads, inert edges, output projections and family maps of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], joins and relative limit diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $q:E^\otimes\to O^\otimes$ be an inert-preserving map of symmetric infinity-operads over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. Let $v\in E^\otimes$ have arity $s\geq0$, let $I=\{1,\ldots,s\}$ be discrete, and choose inert projections $v\to v_i$ over every color projection $\rho_i:\langle s\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$. Let $c:\Delta^0\star I\to E^\otimes$ be the specified cone with these edges and apex $v$. Then $c$ is a $q$-limit diagram. More explicitly, for every test object $z\in E^\otimes$ its projection maps induce the following weak homotopy equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(z,v)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{O^\otimes}(qz,qv)\mathbin{\times^h_{\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{O^\otimes}(qz,qv_i)}}\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(z,v_i)$$
The homotopies are those of the specified cone and its image under $q$, retained with all higher simplices in the path-pullback model. For $s=0$ both products are points, so $\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(z,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_{O^\otimes}(qz,qv)$ is an equivalence. No fibration property of $q$ or existence of other limits is assumed.

proof.text: The image under $q$ of each specified inert projection $v\to v_i$ is the corresponding inert projection $qv\to qv_i$ over $\rho_i$, because $q$ is inert-preserving. Thus the image cone $q c$ has the same discrete boundary shape and the same base cone in $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$; all comparison maps below use the homotopies supplied by this specified cone. The empty case $s=0$ has the unique empty boundary and no projection edges.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (3), printed p.341: inert output projections and their image under the operad map

proof.text: Fix a test object $z$ of $E^\otimes$. Apply the limit half of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] to the specified cone $c$. Since $I$ is discrete, restriction to its boundary identifies the upper row with $\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(z,v)\to\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(z,v_i)$, and identifies the lower row with the analogous map for $O^\otimes$; the path-pullback comparison retains the cone homotopy and all higher simplices. Consequently it suffices to prove that this square is a homotopy pullback for every $z$.

source.place: Relative-limit constant-source test, Proposition 7.1.6.19 and its limit dual

proof.text: Let $\phi$ be a pointed map from the arity of $z$ to $\langle s\rangle$. The mapping spaces over $\phi$ in $E^\otimes$ and in $O^\otimes$ are Kan fibers by [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber]. The symmetric-operad Segal axiom says that mapping spaces over any pointed map split as products over its non-basepoint outputs ([lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]); applied to the chosen inert projections, it gives weak equivalences $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_{E}(z,v)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}_{E}(z,v_i)$ and $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_{O}(qz,qv)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}_{O}(qz,qv_i)$. These equivalences form a commutative square because $q$ preserves the projections. In the path-pullback model, the second equivalence identifies the homotopy pullback of the right-hand vertical map with the product on the upper right: compare the two spans by the identity on the upper-right product, the lower Segal equivalence, and the identity on the lower product, and apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]; the resulting path pullback of the identity of the lower product against the upper-right product receives the upper-right product by constant paths, and this inclusion is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], because an identity map is a Kan fibration. Since the arity mapping space is discrete, the $\phi$-fibre of the path pullback is exactly the path pullback of the $\phi$-fibres, paths in the lower product staying over the discrete tuple $(\rho_i\phi)_i$. Composing with the first Segal equivalence proves that the comparison on the $\phi$-fiber is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (3), printed p.341: the two output-Segal mapping-space equivalences and pullback comparison

proof.text: The arity mapping spaces in $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ are discrete, and the maps of mapping spaces to them are Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber]. The full square of Step 2 is therefore a disjoint union of its homotopy-fiber squares indexed by $\phi$. The path pullback of Step 2 is a Kan complex by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], and over a vertex of a discrete space the homotopy fibre is the strict fibre, since every path in a discrete space is constant. By Step 3 every such fiber map is a weak equivalence, so [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], with the identity on the discrete indexing space, makes the full comparison a weak equivalence. This proves that $c$ is a $q$-limit diagram. If $s=0$, the products in the Segal mapping axiom are empty products; each fiber comparison in Step 3 is then the equivalence from the mapping space to the corresponding base mapping space, and the same assembly proves the asserted nullary clause.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q100-c173c7965 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the item and every cited node statement. The split is a correct four-step fibrewise proof of a true statement, and the statement is unchanged. Step 1: inert preservation sends v→v_i to inert projections qv→qv_i (elementary). Step 2: the limit half of lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test needs no fibration hypothesis on q; for discrete I the right-pinched mapping space in Fun(I,-) is the product. Step 3: the Segal splitting over φ, cited from the statement clause of lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition, which matches the definition used via def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family. kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance applies with a=Segal_O, b=c=id. Step 4: fibre detection over the discrete Map_{N(Fin_*)}(<n>,<s>) with v=id. The cases s=0 (empty products, contractible fibres) and s=1 check out. One repairable fault, a missing citation used in two places: step 3 identifies P(id,B_φ) with B_φ, and step 4 needs the path pullback P to be a Kan complex for the fibre-detection hypotheses; neither was cited. I fixed both by citing lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison (same unit, no cycle) and added it to proof_deps. I also wrote out that over a discrete base the homotopy fibre is the strict fibre. Route: all deps are in sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, with no tool_uses and no SGA. No duplicate of the item exists (checked against lem-coef-inert-relative-tuple-cone, lem-coef-symmetric-relative-product-comparison and lem-coef-operadic-operation-segal-product). No new nodes. HA 3.1.2.3 is not archived (the report lists it as WANTED); I checked the argument against the standard p-limit pasting.
